correctness.rationale: All moduli, including 1, 2 and powers of two, are covered. Direct elimination gives a unique y for each simple square root of minus one at split odd prime powers; nonsplit primes and 4 forbid common roots. CRT yields R(m), and p^{-2e} normalized counts give independent local valuations. A uniform large-prime union bound proves tightness, with prime divisor p≤2N+1. The local Euler-product moment calculation converges for t<1; at t=1 the split-prime factor is exactly 1+2/p and the product diverges by the classical reciprocal-prime divergence in the progression 1 mod 4. Exact direct enumerations for m≤129 corroborate but do not prove the infinite result.

value.rationale: Two neighboring norms on a diagonal Gaussian-lattice step have a natural coprimality and common-divisor statistic. The result classifies every integer-valued fiber of their limiting GCD, not only density one/coprimality, and exhibits the nonobvious phenomenon that a finite almost-sure integer limit can have infinite mean. The threshold t=1 is a structural feature of infinitely many split primes, and the precise local factors can be reused for divisor and moment questions.
